remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
The elimination of engineers was one of the wilder hypotheses out there. Just like absurdly wrong. We just gave engineers a power tool that can accelerate the development of whatever we want. 

Of course their value not only remains critical in that world, but actually goes up in many domains because we can apply engineering to far more work than before.

If you’re trying to automate drug discovery, you need engineers. If you’re trying to automate manufacturing, you need engineers. If you’re taking on larger and larger software projects, you need engineers.

This will happen in domains beyond engineering too. AI causes companies to take on way more work than before, which leads to needing more experts to oversee the work. 

Even as models get better and better, they can be better utilized by the experts in those fields than the novices. Great time to be an expert.
remarks.translation: 关于工程师将被淘汰的说法，是当时流传的较为疯狂的假设之一。简直错得离谱。我们只是给了工程师一件可以加速开发任何我们想要之物的强力工具。当然，在那个世界里，他们的价值不仅依然至关重要，而且在许多领域实际上还会上升，因为我们可以将工程应用于比以前多得多的工作。如果你试图自动化药物发现，你需要工程师。如果你试图自动化制造业，你需要工程师。如果你承接越来越大的软件项目，你需要工程师。这种情况也会发生在工程以外的领域。人工智能促使公司承担比以前多得多的工作，这导致需要更多专家来监督这些工作。即使模型变得越来越好，这些领域的专家也能比新手更好地利用它们。现在正是成为专家的好时代。

remarks.name: Nikunj Kothari
remarks.role: partner fpvventures - investing in seed/A. previous: early hire meter, opendoor, atlassian & others. love shimoleejhaveri + 👦👧
remarks.text:
Grok Bot is a fantastic release.. the UX, the design, the onboarding :chefs-kiss:

But I go back and forth on this a lot: Will users (personal and business) want one super agent that holds all the context or sub agents that are designated to do a slice of tasks?

If we treat agents as humans, then the Grok Bot design makes a ton of sense. It allows us to compartmentalize tools, context, outcomes for that person’s division. You reach out to that bot for that specific goal that you have in mind. 

But, if you treat agents as Jarvis, you want a master agent that just gets the job done. It might create and coordinate all the bots (and dare I say the communication/context) that might be needed to do the task. But the interface is 1:1 vs. 1:many. 

My guess is it’ll veer towards the one master agent over time who can then act as an orchestrator who reads / understands the bots you create. But starts narrow as most of the companies are doing it now. 

PS: I understand the core engineering constraints (context windows, tool use, simplicity, cost etc) why companies are choosing task/singular outcomes today. Primarily thinking this from a design / product side.
remarks.translation: Grok Bot 是一次出色的发布……用户体验、设计、引导流程：堪称完美 :chefs-kiss: 但我经常在这两者之间反复纠结：用户（个人和企业）会想要一个掌握所有上下文的超级代理，还是想要被指定去完成一部分任务的子代理？如果我们把代理当作人来对待，那么 Grok Bot 的设计就非常合理。它让我们能够为那个人的部门划分工具、上下文和结果。你带着心中特定的目标去找那个机器人。但是，如果你把代理当作 Jarvis，你就会想要一个能把事情办成的主代理。它可能会创建并协调完成任务所需的所有机器人（甚至包括沟通/上下文）。但界面是 1 对 1，而不是 1 对多。我的猜测是，随着时间推移，它会倾向于一个主代理，这个主代理随后可以充当编排者，读取/理解你创建的机器人。但就像现在大多数公司所做的那样，起步会很窄。附言：我理解核心工程上的限制（上下文窗口、工具使用、简单性、成本等），这也是为什么公司现在选择任务/单一结果。我主要是从设计/产品角度来思考这个问题。

podcasts.originalTitle: Microsoft’s Vision for an Internet Made for Agents With CTO Kevin Scott (Best of the Pod)
podcasts.excerpt: 2025年，凯文·斯科特押注智能体网络将成为人工智能领域的下一件大事。这位微软首席技术官认为，要让智能体真正有用，它们需要能够代表我们采取行动——这意味着要让它们访问构成互联网的同样庞杂的工具、数据和系统。如今，这一赌注开始见效，因为智能体网络的基础设施正在建设中。在本周的AI & I节目中，丹·希珀重温了他与凯文的对话。他们讨论了微软在智能体网络中的角色、为什么开放性不必以牺牲安全性为代价，以及为什么程序员应该对新工具保持好奇，而不是出于原则而抵制它们。如果你觉得这期节目有趣，请点赞、订阅、评论并分享！想了解更多丹·希珀的内容：订阅Every：https://…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: In 2025, Kevin Scott bet that the agentic web would be the next big thing in AI.The Microsoft CTO argued that for agents to be genuinely useful, they'd need to be able to take action on our behalf—which would mean giving them access to the same sprawl of tools, data, and systems that make up the internet. Today, that bet is starting to pay off, as the foundational infrastructure for the agentic web is now being built.On this week's AI & I, Dan Shipper revisits his conversation with Kevin. They discuss Microsoft's role in the agentic web, why openness doesn't have to come at the expense of security, and why programmers should stay curious about new tools rather than resist them on principle.If you found this episode interesting, please like, subscribe, comment, and share!To hear more from Dan Shipper:Subscribe to Every: https://…
